(a) selection-only vs tool-default, confirmed per-listener by reading each called setter's own body (all setter bodies are out of scope, timeline.js:608-842): `applyStrokeGradAlongToSelection` (10398-10404) is genuinely selection-ONLY — it early-returns `if(!selectedPaths.length)return;` (10399) and never writes any `state.*` field, matching its own 10393-10397 lead-in's claim that this property has 'no meaningful future-stroke default.' By contrast `#fill-enable-toggle`/`#stroke-enable-toggle` (10436-10437) call `setFillEnabled`/`setStrokeEnabled` (timeline.js:647/654), which unconditionally write `state.fillEnabled`/`state.strokeEnabled` (the TOOL default for the next stroke) and ONLY THEN, conditionally, also touch `selectedPaths` when `state.tool` is `'select'`/`'subselect'` and a selection exists. The packet-2 hex/alpha fields (`setFillColor`/`setStrokeColor`, timeline.js:608/615) follow the exact same tool-default-plus-conditional-selection shape. `setCanvasSize` (packet 3, timeline.js:842) is a THIRD category: pure document-level state (`state.canvasW/H`), with no selection concept at all. The packet-4 plain fields split further: `setOpacity` (timeline.js:799) is called out in its OWN comment (10-line block starting just after its declaration, out of scope) as historically NOT applying to selection at all, unlike `setFillColor`/`setStrokeColor`; `setStrokeCap`/`setStrokeJoin`/`setMiterLimit`/`setDashOffset`/`setStrokeStyle`/`setPaintOrder` (timeline.js:717-727) all follow the tool-default-plus-conditional-selection shape; `setFillBrushMode` (timeline.js:788) is tool-default ONLY (`state.fillBrushMode=v;` with no selection branch); `smoothSelectedStroke` (10550, timeline.js:741) is selection-ONLY, mirroring `applyStrokeGradAlongToSelection`'s own shape (early-returns if no selection).
(b) see (a) above for the full precedence/target table across every setter this scope's listeners call.

(c) the three hex helpers, `hexDisplayValue`/`alphaPctFromHex`/`parseHexInput` (10442-10462), are pure input->output functions with no DOM/state access of their own — see `reconciliation` above for the `.dataset.hex8` scoping finding (the token never appears as a property access anywhere in this scope).

(d) dimensions-lock: `_dimsLockRatio` (10495) starts `null`; `#btn-dims-lock` click (10496-10499) toggles a `.on` CSS class on itself and captures the ratio `state.canvasW/state.canvasH` into `_dimsLockRatio` ONLY at the moment it is switched ON (10499: `_dimsLockRatio=on?(...):null`), never re-captured while already on. While locked, `#p-cw` input (10508-10515) derives `h=Math.max(1,Math.round(parseFloat(this.value)/_dimsLockRatio))` and mirrors it into `#p-ch`'s own `.value` (10512) BEFORE calling `window.SM.setCanvasSize(w,h)` (10514); `#p-ch` input (10516-10523) is the exact mirror, multiplying instead of dividing (10519) and mirroring into `#p-cw` (10520). When unlocked, each field passes the OTHER dimension through unchanged from live `state.canvasW`/`state.canvasH` (10509/10517) and still calls `setCanvasSize` unconditionally (10514/10522) — the 2026-08-31 feedback-#188 comment (10501-10507) explains this unconditional call is itself the fix: these two listeners pre-existed but only acted when the ratio link was on, so with the link off the resize did not apply until the drag's final native `change` fired.

(e) initial-paint block (10524-10537): `window.SM.setFillColor(state.fillColor)`/`setFillEnabled(state.fillEnabled)`/`setStrokeEnabled(state.strokeEnabled)` (10527-10529) read the three named `state.*` fields and re-run their own setters purely to paint the panel's swatches from whatever `state` already holds at script-load time — per the 10524-10526 comment, without this the swatch would show the static HTML's own background (transparent) until first touched. `if(window.ColorPicker){...}` (10530-10537) is a presence guard: `ColorPicker` (color-picker.js) is loaded via its own `<script>` tag elsewhere in index.html and exports `window.ColorPicker` only after that file runs, so this guard tolerates a load-order change or the file being stripped from a build without throwing. The four `window.SM.setTool('eyedropper')` calls (10532-10535) are NOT initial-paint calls — they are `onEyedrop` callbacks registered with `ColorPicker.wireColorSwatches` (color-picker.js:259-273, out of scope) and run LATER, only when the user clicks the eyedropper icon inside that specific colour-well's own popover (opened by a click on `#stroke-well`/`#pm-stroke`/`#fill-well`/`#pm-fill`), switching the active tool so the next canvas click samples a colour for that specific target field; the two `onNone` callbacks (10534-10535, fill wells only) call `window.SM.setFillEnabled(false)` when the popover's 'None' option is picked.

(f) icon-group mechanism (10556-10577): `wireIconGroup(wrapId,setterName)` (10556-10564) adds ONE click listener to the wrap element; on a click that hits a `.icon-btn` descendant (`e.target.closest('.icon-btn')`, 10559), it toggles the `sel` CSS class (`classList.toggle('sel', b===btn)`, 10560 — NOT an `ac` class) on every button so exactly one carries `sel`, mirrors the clicked button's own `data-value` onto the wrap's own `wrap.dataset.value` (10561), and calls `window.SM[setterName](btn.dataset.value)` (10562). `paintIconGroup(wrapId,value)` (10565-10569) is the read-side inverse: given a value, it writes `wrap.dataset.value` and toggles `sel` on whichever button's own `data-value` matches. The four wrap ids and their setters (10570-10573): `p-cap-grp`->`setStrokeCap`, `p-join-grp`->`setStrokeJoin`, `p-paintorder-grp`->`setPaintOrder`, `p-fillbrushmode-grp`->`setFillBrushMode`; the four matching initial `paintIconGroup` calls (10574-10577) seed each from `state.strokeCap`/`state.strokeJoin`/`state.paintOrder`/`state.fillBrushMode`. External callers of `paintIconGroup`, found by grep restricted to `src/`: `_restoreDrawingDefaults()` (timeline.js:3525-3539, out of scope) repaints `p-cap-grp`/`p-join-grp`/`p-paintorder-grp` from a snapshotted TOOL-default state when leaving a drawing tool; `updateSelPropsPanel()` (timeline.js:3547-3679, out of scope) repaints the same three groups from the newly-selected path's OWN `strokeCap`/`strokeJoin`/`data.paintOrder` on every selection change (3678-3679), and also calls `syncStrokePropsForVectorBrush()` (timeline.js:3510, inside `updatePropsContext()`, timeline.js:3131) as 'the single per-selection decider' per this scope's own 10551-10555/10645-10646 comments. `wireIconGroup` itself has no external callers (only the four calls at 10570-10573, confirmed by grep).

(g) the three enable-sync functions, as a precedence table: `syncMiterLimitEnabled()` (10581) sets `#p-miterlimit`'s own `.disabled` to true unless `#p-join-grp`'s own `dataset.value==='miter'`; triggered by a click on `#p-join-grp` (10582) and once eagerly at load (10583). `syncJoinEnabledForGradient()` (10601-10609) sets `grp-disabled` class AND `title` on `#p-join-grp` when `#p-strokegrad-along` is checked, and additionally force-disables `#p-miterlimit` in that case (10608) or defers back to `syncMiterLimitEnabled()` otherwise; triggered by `#p-strokegrad-along`'s own `change` (10610) and once eagerly (10611). `syncStrokePropsForVectorBrush()` (10631-10654) sets `grp-disabled`+`title`+`dataset.brushOff='1'` on BOTH `#p-cap-grp` and `#p-join-grp` (plus `.disabled`+`title` on `#p-strokestyle`) when the ENTIRE selection is vector-brush strokes (`anyBrush&&!anyOther`, 10633-10640) — a mixed selection is deliberately left untouched (10637-10639 comment) because ordinary paths in that selection still need the controls live. Ownership marker (`dataset.brushOff`, 10643-10650): the join group is shared between the gradient reason and the brush reason; `syncStrokePropsForVectorBrush` only clears `grp-disabled` off `#p-join-grp` when IT was the one that set it (`g.dataset.brushOff==='1'`, 10649) and, when clearing, re-invokes `syncJoinEnabledForGradient()` (10650) so the gradient's own reason (if still active) re-asserts itself instead of being silently dropped — the inverse guard (10647: `if(id==='p-join-grp'&&!off&&g.dataset.brushOff!=='1')return;`) means `syncStrokePropsForVectorBrush` never overwrites a disabled-reason it did not itself set. `syncStrokePropsForVectorBrush` has one external caller: `updatePropsContext()` (timeline.js:3510, out of scope) and is also exported as `window.syncStrokePropsForVectorBrush` (10655) for that external call to reach it (the other two sync functions have no external callers, confirmed by grep — both are only referenced by their own click/change hooks and by each other's own rationale comments).

packets.responsibility: Defines the shared selection-mutation helper for the stroke-gradient-along-path feature and wires its three DOM listeners, then wires the two legacy (non-Figma-row) Fill/Stroke enable-toggle clicks. `applyStrokeGradAlongToSelection(mutate)` (10398-10404) is a selection-only helper: it early-returns if nothing is selected (10399), otherwise pushes ONE undo step (10400), applies the caller's `mutate` callback to every path in `selectedPaths` (10401), saves the active layer frame and calls `updateUI()` (10402), and finally re-renders via `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` if the Rust engine is active (10403) — the ONLY render/undo/persistence call in this whole packet. `#p-strokegrad-along` change (10405-10416) either sets `p.data.strokeGradientAlongPath={from,to}` reading the two colour-stop inputs' plain `.value` (10412-10413) when checked, or deletes the data field when unchecked. `#p-strokegrad-from-c`/`#p-strokegrad-to-c` input (10417-10435) each live-paint their own swatch background from `this.value` and then update ONLY the matching `from`/`to` field on paths that already carry `strokeGradientAlongPath`, no-op otherwise. The trailing `#fill-enable-toggle`/`#stroke-enable-toggle` clicks (10436-10437) are the 'left tool-panel' half of the two-eye-icon mirror described at timeline.js:625-633 (out of scope, same file) — they call `window.SM.setFillEnabled`/`setStrokeEnabled` with the boolean flip of the CURRENT `state.fillEnabled`/`state.strokeEnabled`.
callers: `applyStrokeGradAlongToSelection` is called exactly THREE times, all internal to this same packet and none external: 10407 (inside the `#p-strokegrad-along` change listener), 10420 (inside the `#p-strokegrad-from-c` input listener), 10428 (inside the `#p-strokegrad-to-c` input listener) — confirmed by a whole-repo grep restricted to call sites, excluding its own declaration.

`setFillEnabled`/`setStrokeEnabled` (timeline.js:647/654, out of scope) are called from many other sites across timeline.js/app.js/tools.js/tutorial.js; within THIS packet they are called only at 10436/10437.
`window.SMEngineBridge.renderNow` (out of scope, engine-bridge.js) is guarded by `if(window.SMEngineBridge)` (10403) — the same optional-engine guard used throughout the codebase.

packets.signature: function hexDisplayValue(hex); function alphaPctFromHex(hex); function parseHexInput(raw); document.getElementById('p-fill-hex').addEventListener('change',fn); document.getElementById('p-stroke-hex').addEventListener('change',fn); document.getElementById('p-stroke-alpha').addEventListener('input',fn); ['p-fill-hex','p-stroke-hex'].forEach(fn);
packets.responsibility: Three pure hex-string helper functions (no DOM/state access of their own) plus the Figma-style inline hex/alpha text-field listeners that use them. `hexDisplayValue(hex)` (10442-10446): strips '#' (defaulting to '#000000'), and if the result is 8 hex digits whose last byte is 'FF' (case-insensitive), drops that byte — the FF-drop rule — always returns uppercase. `alphaPctFromHex(hex)` (10449-10453): returns 100 unless the stripped hex is exactly 8 digits, in which case it parses the last byte as 0-255 and rounds `(byte/255)*100` to the nearest integer percent. `parseHexInput(raw)` (10457-10462): trims and strips a leading '#'; a 3-digit input is digit-doubled ('abc'->'#AABBCC'); a 6- or 8-digit input is passed through uppercased with '#' prepended; anything else (mid-typing) returns `null`. `#p-fill-hex`/`#p-stroke-hex` change (10463-10474) each parse `this.value`; on failure they reset the field's own displayed value via `hexDisplayValue(state.fillColor/strokeColor)` and return without calling any setter (so an invalid typed string snaps back to the last valid colour); on success they call `window.SM.setFillColor/setStrokeColor(hex)` and, if the fill/stroke is currently disabled, also force it enabled. `#p-stroke-alpha` input (10479-10485) clamps the typed percent to 0-100, computes a 2-digit hex alpha byte from it, and calls `setStrokeColor` with the RGB unchanged and the alpha byte appended ONLY if pct<100 (10483) — matching `hexDisplayValue`'s own FF-drop rule by construction (never writing an explicit 'FF'). Lines 10486-10489 add a shared Enter-to-blur handler to both hex fields so pressing Enter commits the typed value (native 'change' fires on blur).
